atoms.a: They wanted to watch TV but they hadn’t finished their homework.
atoms.b: They wanted to watch TV ((but)) they hadn’t finished their homework.

instruction.text: Is this a coordinating or subordinating conjunction?

hint.text: Subordinating conjunctions come before clauses that do not make sense on their own. Coordinating conjunctions join two clauses together that can both make sense on their own.

atoms.a: Paul doesn’t like maths because it is tricky.
atoms.b: Paul doesn’t like maths ((because)) it is tricky.

atoms.a: You can do your English homework or you can work on your History project.
atoms.b: You can do your English homework ((or)) you can work on your History project.

instruction.text: Is this a coordinating or subordinating conjunction?

hint.text: Subordinating conjunctions come before clauses that do not make sense on their own. Coordinating conjunctions join two clauses together that can both make sense on their own.

finish.text: A coordinating conjunction is a word that can join two main clauses together to make a complex sentence.
A subordinating conjunction is a word that can join a main clause and a subordinate clause together to make a complex sentence.
